    Endomorphism dimension drops under nonsplit extension #

    This file formalizes the dimension comparison used in Ringel Section 2.3, Lemma 1. Exactness bounds Hom dimensions for the middle term by those for the two endpoints. If the extension is nonsplit, one of these bounds is strict, hence replacing the endpoints by the middle term strictly lowers the endomorphism dimension, even in the presence of an unchanged direct summand.

    source
    theorem MagnitudeConjecture.LinearMap.finrank_le_add_of_exact {k : Type u} [Field k] {U V W : Type v} [AddCommGroup U] [AddCommGroup V] [AddCommGroup W] [Module k U] [Module k V] [Module k W] [FiniteDimensional k U] [FiniteDimensional k V] [FiniteDimensional k W] (f : U →ₗ[k] V) (g : V →ₗ[k] W) (hfg : Function.Exact ⇑f ⇑g) :
    Module.finrank k V ≤ Module.finrank k U + Module.finrank k W

    Exactness at the middle term gives the elementary dimension bound dim V ≤ dim U + dim W.

    source

    If the second map in an exact pair is not onto, the middle dimension bound is strict.

    A short exact pair of linear maps gives additivity of finite dimensions.

    Reorganize a finite biproduct by displaying two distinct summands first and collecting all remaining summands in a complementary biproduct.

      Ringel Section 2.3, Lemma 1 in the form needed for the minimization argument: replacing two summands by a nonsplit extension strictly lowers the endomorphism dimension even after adjoining an arbitrary unchanged summand.
